ok I'm so mad I can barely type straight so bear with me

the switchblade moth from my sept flash day is being sold as a vinyl sticker by a shop called StickerBurrow Co. "Knife Moth Vinyl Decal," $6.50 or 3 for $15. same crack in the blade, same wing pattern. they didn't even flip it. it's a straight scan of my linework, not "inspired by," mine.

I drew that whole sheet at my kitchen table over three weekends. posted it aug 30 and that moth was gone in the first hour of flash day. flash is one design, sold one time, to one person. that's the whole deal, and the person who got it paid for that piece.

so I messaged them. the reply was "love your work!" then "moths are a very common tattoo motif" and "send a registered copyright through our support form." so basically pound sand.

copyright exists the second you draw something. registration is just the paperwork you need if you want to take someone to court. I know small shops don't have lawyer money and these sticker places know it. that's exactly why they do it.

also, a client messaged me tonight thinking I was the one selling stickers of her tattoo. to whoever that was: it was not me. I would never sell a piece that already belongs to somebody else. if you got one of my pieces and you're worried about this, DM me and we'll sort it out.

if you see that listing, report it through whatever site it's on for copyright infringement. don't buy from them. if you're a tattoo person reading this, you already know why this matters. we spend years learning to draw this stuff and people just take it.

rant over, I'm gonna go stare at the wall for a while.
